items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: He finally took us over and called us Edgar Pillows' Night Owls.

ctx.x: Around 1925, I was downtown one day and they were building the Capital Theater on Grand Avenue. I had gone to the music store and bought an orchestration on "Aggravating Papa," I think it was. And as I was going home there was a hod carrier who came over to me you know, put his stick there and said, hey, son, what's that you've got? Music? I said, "yes." He said, "well, let me see it." I showed it to him and he said, "well, could I have a second trumpet part, do you have it? I said, "yes," because we didn't have…

His name was Edgar Pillows (PHONETIC) and he was an older man. He came up one day and he heard us rehearse. He got himself an E flat tuba and started rehearsing with us. He finally took us over and called us Edgar Pillows' Night Owls. It was just the five of us. No, we had one more man, older man, which was a banjo player, Emery Henry Green. So it was Edgar Pillows who was the leader, Emery Henry Green the banjo player and --
